THE IDEA

A pin should tell you more.

Finding a place is only the first step. The useful part is understanding what kind of place it is, how strong the information is, and whether anyone has checked it recently.

FROM LANDING PAGE TO APP

One visual language.
Every place, in context.

Try two sample states. Labels, shape, and wording change together, so the difference is clear beyond color alone.

02 / THE APP EXPERIENCE

The status leads.
The map follows.

A place card puts the evidence status, latest check, and access note first, before anyone considers directions. A community report never reads like a designated area.

RELEASE PLANS

The next stop is getting it ready.

The shared API is implemented, an iOS pilot runs in a simulator, and an Android pilot client is in development. Public release work remains, with Android planned first. Neither app is available in the stores yet.
